steps: Open Settings → AI generation and choose the Work verification preference: Ask every time, Automatic, or Off.
Complete the implementation from the linked task, doc, or approved plan. Read the agent result and inspect its changed files before treating any summary as proof that the requirements are met.
When Verify this work? appears, choose Verify now for this result. Not now skips the current offer. Always verify also changes the future preference; Never verify turns the preference off.

Let the verification pass finish and read the requirement-level outcomes. Met means the verifier found supporting evidence; Missed identifies an unmet requirement; Unclear needs clarification or additional evidence.
If Ask to fix is available, review the clear misses and use it to request the focused corrections. Do not assume an unclear requirement has automatically become an implementation task.
After the fix pass, use Re-verify when prompted, or let Automatic mode run it. Inspect the latest result and any remaining uncertainty.
Perform the relevant manual checks and delivery review before shipping. Verification is another agent pass, not a guarantee that every runtime or product behavior was exercised.
outcome: You have a visible record of how the implementation compares with its written requirements and can follow a fix-and-recheck cycle.
troubleshooting: If no offer appears, check the setting, whether the conversation actually changed files, and whether it has a linked task/doc or implemented plan. An ordinary unlinked question, delegated specialist conversation, or design handoff may not meet the same eligibility rules. Verification takes additional time and provider usage. Clarify vague requirements before asking the agent to guess the intended behavior.

title: Understand how Choro Remote connects to your Mac
summary: Understand which device runs your work and what must stay online when you use Choro Remote.
before: Have Choro on your Mac and Choro Remote on your iPhone. Add your projects and connect a coding provider on the Mac before expecting them to appear on the phone.
steps: Think of the phone as a control for your Mac workspace. Agents, project files, coding-provider credentials, and terminal processes continue to run on the Mac.
Open Desktop Settings → Remote access and connect the Mac. Choro and the phone communicate through the relay; the phone does not need an inbound port opened on your Mac.
Pair the phone using the Mac ID and a current one-time pairing code. Each paired device has its own access level and can be revoked independently.
Keep the Mac awake, online, and running Choro while you use Remote. An offline Mac cannot receive a new instruction merely because the phone has an internet connection.
Use the phone to monitor conversations and, when permitted, send work or respond to decisions. Review the selected project and conversation before taking an action.
Return to the Mac for workflows that are not available in the mobile interface. Remote does not move your repository or its running services into a cloud agent.
outcome: You know where work executes and how the phone reaches it, so you can distinguish a connection problem from an agent problem.
troubleshooting: Application messages are encrypted between the paired devices, but the relay can still observe connection metadata. Pairing is not a backup or a repository sync. If a project is absent, first confirm that it exists in the connected Mac workspace. If the Mac is asleep or Choro has closed, restore that connection before retrying an instruction.

title: Pair your iPhone
summary: Connect an iPhone to the intended Mac using a short-lived pairing code.
before: Open Choro on the Mac you want to control and Choro Remote on the phone. Keep both devices online and have physical access to the Mac’s Remote access settings.
steps: On the Mac, open Settings → Remote access. In Pair a phone, choose Connect & pair and wait for the connection and pairing details.
Read the Mac ID and the active pairing code. The code is one-time and expires after five minutes; generate a New code if the current one expires.
On the phone, open Connect to your Mac. Enter the Mac ID in MAC ID and the current code in PAIRING CODE.
Choose Pair securely and wait for the project list. Do not repeatedly submit while pairing is still in progress.
On the Mac, confirm that the new device appears in the paired-device list. Give it only the access level you intend it to have.
Open a familiar project and conversation on the phone to confirm that you paired the intended workspace. Keep Choro running on the Mac.
outcome: The phone can reconnect to the paired Mac and see the projects its connection is authorized to access.
troubleshooting: An expired or already-used code requires a new pairing window. Check the Mac ID separately from the code; they serve different purposes. If pairing fails, read the exact error, verify that the Mac’s remote connection is on, and check both devices’ network connections. Do not publish a live pairing code in a screenshot or support request.

title: Choose a device’s access level
summary: Choose whether a paired phone can only observe work, control agents, or approve more powerful actions.
before: Pair the phone first and open Settings → Remote access on the Mac. Device permissions and the access mode selected for an individual agent are separate controls.
steps: Find the intended phone in the paired-device list. Check its name and pairing information before changing access.
Click its permission label to cycle through View only, Control, and Full access. Stop when the displayed label matches your intended choice.
Use View only for monitoring. The phone can read information but requests that mutate the workspace are refused.

Use Control for ordinary agent work such as starting or continuing a conversation and answering questions. Control cannot select the agent’s Full access mode or approve actions reserved for the device’s Full access tier.
Use Full access only when that phone should also resolve command approvals, select unrestricted agent access, or ship work. These actions can affect files and remote repositories.
Return to the phone and confirm that the intended action is available. If the phone reports a permission error, check this device setting before changing an unrelated model or provider setting.
outcome: The paired phone has an explicit permission level that matches how you intend to use it.
troubleshooting: A phone may display an action that the Mac subsequently refuses: permission is checked by the Mac when the request arrives. Upgrading a device does not repair provider authentication or repository permissions. For a phone that should no longer connect at all, use Revoke instead of merely changing its tier.

title: Monitor agent progress from your phone
summary: Find the conversations running on your Mac and recognize when they need your attention.
before: Use a paired phone and keep the Mac online with Choro open. View only access is sufficient for monitoring.
steps: Open Remote and check the connection line at the top. Choro Desktop on Mac indicates the connected state; Reconnecting to Mac means the view may not yet reflect new activity.
Expand the project containing the work. Projects show their conversations, with recent activity listed first.
Use Search agents to find a conversation by its title or project name. If a project has many conversations, use Show more agents to reveal the rest.
Open the conversation and read the latest messages, work activity, and status. A running indicator shows ongoing work; a highlighted attention state means a decision may be waiting.
Read any question, plan, approval, or final result before deciding what to do next. Monitoring alone does not answer a pending question or approve a command.
Return to the project list to check other work. If a conversation’s state differs from the Mac, recheck connectivity before starting a duplicate task.
outcome: You can keep track of several Mac conversations from the phone and identify which ones need a response.
troubleshooting: An old activity timestamp is not necessarily an error; the conversation may simply be idle. Mac unavailable and Reconnecting to Mac are connection states, not proof that an agent failed. An empty project list requires checking the selected Mac workspace rather than recreating the same project from the phone.

title: Start or continue work from your phone
summary: Start a new agent task or send a focused follow-up to an existing conversation from your iPhone.
before: Use a paired phone with Control or Full access, a connected Mac, and a working coding provider on that Mac. The work runs against the Mac project files.
steps: In Projects, find the intended project and choose its New agent action. Confirm the project name in the new-agent screen.
Describe the outcome, relevant files, and any limits. For example, ask the agent to explain navigation without changing files before assigning a larger implementation.
Review the provider, model, effort, and access settings. Select Plan when you want an approach for review before implementation; use Build for work you are ready to start.
Enable Solo if the task should run in its own Git branch and worktree. Check that the project supports that workflow before relying on isolation.
Choose Start agent and wait for its conversation to open. Read any setup error before trying again.
To continue existing work, open its conversation, read the latest result, and send a specific follow-up through the composer.
If you need to interrupt an active pass, use Stop agent and wait for the state to change. Stopping does not automatically undo file edits that already happened.
outcome: The new task or follow-up reaches the intended Mac conversation, where you can monitor progress and respond to decisions.
troubleshooting: If Start agent is unavailable, wait for configuration to load and enter a nonempty prompt. A Control device cannot request Full access for an agent. If connection drops after sending, inspect the conversation on reconnect before submitting the same work again. Provider sign-in and usage errors must be resolved for the provider running on the Mac.

title: Respond to questions, plans, and approvals
summary: Unblock an agent by answering its question, reviewing its plan, or deciding on a requested approval.
before: Open the intended conversation on a connected phone. Control can answer questions and plan decisions; resolving a command approval requires the device’s Full access permission.
steps: When Agent needs your input appears, choose Answer. Read the current question and select the option that matches your intent, or enter a custom answer.
For a group of questions, continue through every question and submit the completed answers. Selecting an option alone does not mean the whole group has been sent.
For a proposed plan, read the plan before using Implement this plan? Choose Yes, implement this plan and then Implement only when its scope is correct.
To request a different approach, enter feedback under No, tell the agent what to do differently and choose Submit. Use Dismiss if you want to close that plan decision without implementing it.
For an approval request, inspect the requested action and its details. Choose Approve to authorize that request or Deny when it should not run.
Wait for the card and conversation state to update. Confirm that work continues or that the agent responds to your feedback before leaving the decision.
outcome: The agent receives an explicit decision for the question, plan, or approval that was blocking its current work.
troubleshooting: Plan implementation and command approval are different decisions. Approving a plan does not mean every later command is automatically approved. If a request was already answered on the Mac, refresh the conversation rather than submitting conflicting decisions. A permission error on an approval usually requires reviewing the phone’s device tier on the Mac.

title: Review results and request fixes
summary: Review an agent’s result on your phone and ask for corrections when the implementation misses a requirement.
before: Open the completed conversation on a connected phone. Reading is available with View only; requesting a fix needs Control or Full access.
steps: Read the final response, reported checks, and any remaining limitations. A completed turn does not by itself establish that the feature works.
Open the changed-file information and select a file to inspect its diff. Compare the actual changes with the task’s requested scope.
Complete the relevant manual checks separately from agent-reported checks. Return to the Mac to use its What to check checklist and test behavior that cannot be assessed on the phone.
If a verification result is present, read its Met, Missed, and Unclear requirements. Use Show all when present to include the met requirements, then read the evidence and unresolved work.
Use Ask to fix when the verification card offers actionable misses. For other issues, send a specific follow-up explaining the expected behavior and what you observed.
Wait for the correction pass, then review the updated changes and any new verification result. Return to the Mac for runtime checks or inspection that cannot be completed meaningfully on the phone.

If you proceed to Ship, review the proposed files, branch, commit, and delivery actions before confirming. Shipping requires the device’s Full access permission and can commit, push, and create a pull request.
outcome: You have reviewed the result and either accepted its evidence or requested a focused correction in the same conversation.
troubleshooting: Unclear means that more evidence or a clearer requirement is needed; it is not equivalent to Met. A diff can confirm code changes without proving the running user experience. If Ask to fix is unavailable, check whether the result contains fixable misses and whether another pass is already running. Do not repeatedly ship when an earlier delivery may already have succeeded.

title: Revoke a paired device
summary: Remove a phone’s authorization to reconnect to your Mac workspace.
before: Open Settings → Remote access on the Mac. Identify the device carefully, especially if several phones have similar names.
steps: Locate the phone in the paired-device list and review its identifying information and access level.
Choose Revoke for that device when you want to remove its authorization.
Confirm that the device is no longer listed as paired. Its existing credentials should no longer grant access to the Mac.
If you have the phone, open Remote and check that it can no longer reconnect using the old pairing.
To authorize that phone again later, start a new pairing window and pair with a fresh code. Review the new device’s permission level afterward.
Use the desktop connection’s Disconnect control when you want to turn remote connectivity off for the Mac as a whole. This is a different choice from revoking one device.
outcome: The selected phone loses its existing authorization while you retain control over other paired devices.
troubleshooting: Disconnecting from the Mac in the phone app clears that phone’s local connection, but revocation on the Mac is the authoritative way to remove its authorization. Revocation does not delete project files or undo work the phone previously requested. If the device disappears while you are reviewing the list, check the current state before acting on another row.

title: Your phone cannot connect to your Mac
summary: Identify whether a Remote connection problem comes from pairing, the Mac’s availability, or the phone’s permission level.
before: Keep the exact message visible on the phone and open Settings → Remote access on the intended Mac. Avoid repeatedly starting the same agent task while connectivity is uncertain.
steps: Check that the Mac is awake, has internet access, and is running Choro. Confirm that Remote access is connected; use Connect if it is off.
Check the phone’s internet connection and the Mac ID used for pairing. A phone connected to a different Mac will not show the expected workspace.
If pairing fails, inspect the active code on the Mac. Generate a New code when it expired or was already used, then enter that current code on the phone.
If an already-paired phone cannot reconnect, check whether its device entry still exists on the Mac. A revoked or expired authorization needs a new pairing.
Distinguish Mac unavailable or Reconnecting to Mac from a permission error. A permission error can occur while connected; check View only, Control, or Full access for that phone.
If projects load but a new agent fails, inspect the provider and project on the Mac. Network pairing does not repair provider sign-in, a missing folder, or a failed worktree setup.
After recovery, read the conversation before resending a request. If the problem persists, record the app versions, connection status, time, exact error, and whether other devices can connect.
outcome: You can narrow the failure to connection, pairing, authorization, or the underlying Mac task and take the matching next step.
troubleshooting: A different Wi-Fi network alone does not require a VPN or opening an inbound Mac port: both devices use the relay. If both devices are online but the relay connection keeps failing, retry after checking network restrictions and service availability. Share diagnostic messages without live pairing codes, tokens, or private project content.
